Groth’s live exact-edition record and Hal Leonard’s official product page independently identify soprano saxophone and piano. The Styrian wind-music association’s GOLD examination repertoire lists Ibert/Nicole Symphonie Concertante for soprano and piano, originally oboe and orchestra. Cyprus’s 2025–2026 music-school performance competition lists the complete work in soprano repertoire. These document teaching/examination contexts; no simplified young-player edition was verified. Only first-page piano and soprano notation previews were inspected. They support concrete demands in the opening movement; they do not establish the whole work’s range or later-movement techniques. research_record.score_observations: Exact AL29268 first soprano-part page: treble clef, common time, Allegro con moto quarter note 138. It begins with long counted rests and rehearsal/cue references before chromatic slurred lines and register changes. The same soprano preview has repeated-note and moving sixteenth-note writing, sixteenth-note triplet groups, rallentando followed by Tempo, and dynamics ranging from pp to ff. These observations concern written B-flat soprano notation, not concert pitch. The AL29268 piano score’s first printed page is headed for oboe and orchestra and has an instrument line. It shows an active chromatic reduction, repeated bass figures, triplets, chordal figures, clef changes and dynamic contrasts. This is not evidence of an authorized saxophone-orchestra version. Teaching inference from the two opening previews: prepare chromatic fingering under slurs, precise entry after counted rests, and coordinated tempo/dynamic transitions with the pianist. Full-work endurance and range require the remaining score.

research_record.identity: Jean-Baptiste Singelée, Cinquième Solo de concert Op.91 for alto saxophone and piano. Linked current edition is Roncorp RON1164, Bruce Ronkin; Adolphe Sax is historical publisher.
research_record.findings: Groth directly identifies RON1164 and editor Bruce Ronkin. This current edition is distinct from the historical Adolphe Sax edition named in the catalog. IMSLP catalogs the original Adolphe Sax plate A.S.95, with six-page score and three-page alto part. Direct PDF retrieval returned verification HTML; Gallica browser access also stopped at security verification. Original notation remains uninspected. The openly displayed Paul Wehage/Musik Fabrik preview is an independent modern edition of this exact alto/piano work. It identifies the 1863 Paris Conservatoire examination context. Swiss Youth Music Competition’s 2026 Sion program names Ethan Merkli performing Cinquième Solo de Concert Op.91. This documents youth competition use without identifying the edition. Sarah Dunbar’s performance upload identifies her as Midwestern State University Assistant Professor of Woodwinds, with guest pianist Ekaterina Chernaya-Oh. This is direct faculty/guest-artist performance evidence alongside youth use. Date conflict: Willemsmusiik’s editor/publisher page explicitly says Composed: 1862; IMSLP work index gives 1863 and Wehage identifies 1863 examination use. These are retained as differing source statements, with no composition date filled.
research_record.score_observations: Visually inspected Wehage’s public opening score page 2 and later score page 5, mm.43-51. These are excerpts of a separate edition, not RON1164 or the original Sax print. The opening score uses common time and Introduction: Allegro. The E-flat alto line has no key signature, against three flats in piano. This is written saxophone notation, not concert-pitch saxophone scoring. Opening saxophone line moves between sustained tones, high-register entries and slurred chromatic runs, with accents and detached repeated notes. Piano initially doubles the contour over repeated bass/chord patterns, then develops more independent treble figures. Later page 5 shows nearly continuous slurred sixteenth-note scalar figures with many accidentals and register changes. Piano has repeated chordal attacks, dolce melodic motion and sustained harmonies. Inference: the solo line needs sustained finger coordination and breath planning through running phrases. The two inspected pages cannot establish full range, every tempo change or all editorial differences between Wehage and Ronkin.

The Brain distributor’s linked TPN1069 preview confirms the Roncorp score title and B-flat soprano staff. Its 1987 copyright is edition metadata, not composition. research_record.score_observations: Inspected the complete one-page Roncorp N1069 public preview, plus opening score pages 2 and 3 of Paul Wehage’s distinct Musik Fabrik edition via its public Sheet Music Plus images. Observations are separated by edition. Roncorp: common time with one flat on the written B-flat soprano staff and three flats in piano. Allegro piano flourish precedes a soprano entry marked Récit. The entry uses accidentals, expressive accents and rising/falling register motion. Roncorp’s m.5 and m.11 areas contain long chromatic sixteenth-note groups interrupted by high fermatas, followed by descending runs. The solo line later moves to più lento with sustained/slurred melody. Piano texture shifts between accented chordal attacks with running treble figures and sparse, separated chords under recitative. Inference: players must coordinate fermatas and flexible timing, rather than maintain an uninterrupted metronomic accompaniment. Wehage’s opening preview explicitly marks the piano recitativo, colla parte, reinforcing the flexible ensemble character in that edition. It is not used to claim identical Ronkin editorial markings. No full range or complete-form analysis is claimed.

research_record.findings: The actual Leduc cover names Jean-Michel Damase, specifies alto saxophone and piano, gives AL 29594 and explicitly prints 1er cycle. This is direct evidence of a teaching-oriented edition. The publisher’s 2018 catalogue separately lists Andantino AL 29507 and Andantino Pastoral AL 29594. Plain Andantino recordings or previews must not be treated as this work. The Centre de Documentation Musicale d’Alsace exact record 5926 verifies AL 29594, alto/piano, three-minute duration, four score pages plus separate parts and 2004 publication. Its local repertoire label is Année 4, with no equivalence established to college study. Broekmans & Van Poppel’s Prima Vista 2007 catalogue lists product 167532 as Andantino pastoral for E-flat alto with accompaniment, 1er cycle, alongside separate product 167531 Andantino. The Tarragona conservatory’s 2025-2026 GP 1 saxophone teaching plan lists Andantino Pastoral by J. M. Damase in its saxophone-and-piano repertoire bibliography. This independently documents conservatory teaching use. No source inspected names an arranger or establishes a prior work from which this edition was simplified. No professional or college performance use was verified. Publication 2004 was not used as a composition year.
